lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Publication, presentation, or reflection: common probabilistic reasoning errors

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Notice how the explanation names the reason for each step.

items.prompt: P(delay | rain) = P(delay). What does that mean?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A box holds 12 items, of which 7 are defective. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are defective, in lowest terms.
Given P(A and B) = 12/20 and P(B) = 13/20, find P(A | B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Given P(A) = 30/100, P(B) = 35/100, and P(A and B) = 18/100, find P(A or B) in lowest terms.
In a study, P(has the condition | tested positive) is much smaller than P(tested positive | has the condition). What is the correct interpretation?
choices: The two conditional probabilities condition on different events, so they need not be close; a rare condition makes the first much smaller.
The two conditional probabilities are equal, so the order of conditioning never matters.
The relationship proves that one event causes the other.
The two events are mutually exclusive.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain your method so that someone who has not done this unit could follow it.
